chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) liked honey.

key_terms.يُعْجِبُهُ: He liked / It was pleasing to him

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) like to eat?
ai.summary: This brief narration from Al-Kafi underscores the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) fondness for honey, a detail that Shia scholars often cite to highlight the medicinal and spiritual virtues of this natural remedy. It connects the Prophet’s personal taste (dhawq) to the broader Islamic tradition of using honey for healing, reinforcing its status as a blessed food mentioned in the Quran. This preference is viewed not merely as a dietary choice but as a sunnah that encourages the consumption of wholesome, divinely inspired substances.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, liked honey a great deal.’”
